companyIntro.name: MedCore Health Partners
companyIntro.mission: Help hospitals use beds, staff and time so patients are treated safely and promptly.
companyIntro.culture: Patient safety first, then flow, then cost. Every metric has a clinical owner.

projectBackground.name: Hospital Flow Programme — City General
projectBackground.context: Emergency patients wait for beds and elective surgery is cancelled. The COO wants facts and a flow plan.

manager.name: Dr. Lena Brandt
manager.role: Director of Operations, MedCore Health Partners
manager.note: Safe flow beats full wards. Show me occupancy, stay and staffing and what you'd change first.

assignment.title: Fix patient flow
assignment.brief: Calculate occupancy, length of stay and staffing, compare wards in Excel and write the bed management plan.

documents.name: Staffing
documents.note: Night shift: 48 patients and 8 nurses; target 1:5.

tasks.title: Bed Occupancy
tasks.prompt: 240 beds with an average of 204 occupied. What is occupancy (%)?
tasks.reasoning: Very high occupancy hurts flow and safety.
tasks.mistake: Chasing 100% leaves no buffer for emergencies.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Average Length of Stay
tasks.prompt: 18,000 patient days and 3,600 discharges. What is ALOS (days)?
tasks.reasoning: ALOS shows how fast patients move through.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Nurses Required
tasks.prompt: 48 patients at a 1:5 nurse ratio. How many nurses are needed (round up)?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Readmission Rate
tasks.prompt: What does a 30-day readmission rate measure?
options: Patients who return to hospital within 30 days of discharge
tasks.reasoning: High readmissions can signal early or poor discharge.
tasks.mistake: Treating all readmissions as failures ignores planned returns.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Ward Occupancy (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Occupancy % in column D = occupied / beds x 100.
tasks.reasoning: ICU and Medical are over-stretched; Surgical has room.
tasks.tip: Move discharge earlier in the day.
tasks.mistake: Reallocating beds without clinical input is unsafe.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Bed Management Plan
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence bed management plan for the COO.
tasks.modelAnswer: Overall occupancy is 85% but ICU runs at 95% and Medical at 90%, which delays emergency admissions. Average stay is 5 days, so we will start discharge planning at admission and move discharges earlier in the day. Night shifts need 10 nurses for 48 patients to meet the 1:5 ratio, two more than rostered. We will review flow metrics weekly and escalate if ICU stays above 90% for three days.
tasks.reasoning: A good plan identifies the constraint, the action, staffing and review triggers.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Midday Discharge
caseStudy.background: A hospital discharged most patients after 4pm. Emergency patients waited in corridors every morning until beds opened.
caseStudy.challenges: Discharges were late in the day.
caseStudy.solution: MedCore introduced a pre-noon discharge target and ward huddles.
